record.what_it_does: Podio is a customizable work and CRM platform with apps, items, tasks and workflows.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization-code flow (user approves, code exchanged for token) is for general clients. A password flow exists for trusted clients only. Tokens are sent as oauth_token. Podio also has app-level auth, which I didn't confirm on a page. Podio's older docs page calls the two-step flow incomplete, so that note may be stale.
record.access_notes: A Podio account plus agreement to the API terms lets you grab an API key from account settings. Rate limits apply, and higher limits are available on request. I did not confirm whether the API needs a paid plan or whether public distribution needs review.
record.api_breadth_notes: The docs describe "a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality" (items, apps, spaces, tasks, files, hooks and more). I didn't count operations. Wrapper libraries exist for several languages.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.podio.com/mcp. It's hosted by Progress, uses OAuth, exposes 22 tools, and is in beta for evaluation and testing. Community servers also exist (Zapier, Pipedream and others).
record.blocker_notes: Nothing blocks a build. Caveats: the vendor's own MCP is still in beta, and the developer docs have moved. developers.podio.com/doc/authentication returned HTTP 410.
